chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man fasted during the journey.' So he said: 'If it had reached him that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that, then upon him is the making up (for it); and if it did not reach him, then there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: the making up (of a missed obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fasting during travel if one is ignorant of the prohibition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia principle of 'bara'ah al-asliyyah' (presumption of innocence) regarding acts of worship, where ignorance of a prohibition exempts one from penalty but not from the obligation of making up the fast (qada). It distinguishes between the ruling for one who was unaware of the Prophet's prohibition versus one who knew, emphasizing that the lack of knowledge removes the specific penalty associated with the transgression. This reflects the broader juristic consensus that ignorance of a ruling does not negate the duty to perform the act correctly once the knowledge is acquired.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man Fasts during the journey’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it had reached him that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from that, so upon him is the making up for it; and if it did not happen to reach him, so there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who fasts on journey.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is informed that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited fasting on a journey, he is required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast) but if such information has not reached him, he is not obligated for anything/”
